review_notes: I read the whole file and looked at each @[simp] lemma and each place where `simp` meets the `qaryEntropy` definition. The binEntropy simp lemmas (`binEntropy_zero`, `binEntropy_one`, `binEntropy_two_inv`, `binEntropy_one_sub`) look fine. `binEntropy_one_sub` only reduces to the argument `p`, so I see no credible loop. Leaving `binEntropy_eq_negMulLog_add_negMulLog_one_sub` out of the simp set is sensible, since it would unfold `binEntropy`. The one concrete problem is the integer-cast form `log (q - 1 : ℤ)`, which conflicts with the simp-set cast lemmas. I did not run Lean, so I make no claim that the proofs were observed to fail. A grep of Mathlib outside this file found no other users of `qaryEntropy`, so the downstream effects are limited to this file. Some uncertainty remains about the best replacement: restating `qaryEntropy_one` with a real-cast RHS, or changing the definition itself.

findings.excerpt: @[simp] lemma qaryEntropy_one (q : ℕ) : qaryEntropy q 1 = log (q - 1 : ℤ) := by simp [qaryEntropy]
findings.problem: The RHS of this simp lemma, `log ((↑(↑q - 1 : ℤ) : ℝ))`, is not in simp normal form. The simp-set lemmas `Int.cast_sub`, `Int.cast_natCast` and `Int.cast_one` rewrite it to `log (↑q - 1)`, so every simp use of the lemma needs a second rewrite step. The definition has the same shape (`log (q - 1 : ℤ)`), and the file works around it in several places. `qaryEntropy_nonneg` calls `simpa [qaryEntropy, -Int.cast_sub]` to stop simp expanding the cast. `deriv_qaryEntropy` and the later derivative statements are written with the real-cast form `log (q - 1)`, and the proof of `deriv_qaryEntropy` needs an explicit `simp only [Int.cast_sub, Int.cast_natCast, Int.cast_one, ...]` to translate between the two forms. The simp interface therefore offers two competing normal forms for the same quantity, the definitional integer-cast one and the real-cast one that simp produces.
findings.proposed_change: State the simp lemma in the form simp actually normalises to, i.e. `qaryEntropy q 1 = log ((q : ℝ) - 1)`. Add a non-simp unfolding lemma such as `qaryEntropy_eq : qaryEntropy q p = p * log ((q : ℝ) - 1) + binEntropy p`, proved by `simp [qaryEntropy]`, and use it in `deriv_qaryEntropy` and `qaryEntropy_nonneg`. Then drop the `-Int.cast_sub` workaround and the manual cast `simp only` list. The integer cast could also be removed from the definition, but the unfolding lemma is the smaller change.
findings.benefit: Simp results on `qaryEntropy q 1` land directly in the form used by `deriv_qaryEntropy`, `hasDerivAt_qaryEntropy` and the `not_continuousAt_*` lemmas, so users get one canonical `log (↑q - 1)` and no cast-normalisation step. The proofs in this file no longer need to suppress `Int.cast_sub` or list cast lemmas by hand.

evidence.excerpt: noncomputable def qaryEntropy (q : ℕ) (p : ℝ) : ℝ := p * log (q - 1 : ℤ) + binEntropy p
